palette.notes: Article's example master palette: 8 hue ramps x 9 swatches plus desaturated neutrals (128 colours); each step brighter shifts hue about +20 degrees so lights drift warm and darks drift cool; saturation peaks mid-ramp and drops near the brightest step. Article figures, not measured.

lighting: Not covered directly; the ramp itself encodes light: dark end cooler and deeper, light end warmer and desaturated, so any shape shaded along one ramp already reads as lit by a warm light.
silhouette: Not covered; the advice is that harmonious, hue-shifted ramps keep separate objects distinct yet unified, which helps a hero stand apart from neutrals.
texture: Neutrals made from the middle of the ramps (flipped and desaturated) fill backgrounds so colourful ramps can be saved for focal objects; texture itself is left to another post.
camera: No camera; scene examples are static.

acting.acts: Staging lesson: a scene reads when backgrounds use the desaturated neutral section and only the subject uses a vivid mid-ramp colour.
acting.depth: Distance can be pushed by stepping toward the neutral, desaturated end of the palette; close things take the saturated middle swatches.

techniques: hue-shifted ramp: about +20 degrees hue per brighter step, lights warm, darks cool
saturation peaks in the middle swatch and falls off toward the brightest step to avoid eye-burning highlights
smaller brightness steps near white, larger saturation steps at both ends
one master ramp rotated 45 degrees around the wheel to make 8 matching ramps
neutral section: middle columns flipped and desaturated for backgrounds
never pure black or pure white unless wanted; never 0 or 100% saturation
feel: one master palette + hue-shifted ramps + desaturated neutrals behind = every colour belongs, hero still pops
for_fred: Build Fred's orange-gold ramp and Pixie's ramp from one shared hue-shifted master (darks toward red-purple, lights toward yellow), and paint backgrounds only from the desaturated neutral row so both characters pop on a busy vertical frame. Avoid bright-and-saturated highlights on Fred's scales.
